title: The crank inside your engine
note: Al-Jazari joined a turning wheel to a connecting rod, and the same crank still runs every engine.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-engineering: 'Al-Jazari served three generations of Artuqid princes as court engineer.' 'The result, the Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices, finished in 1206, is part engineering manual and part illuminated painting: fifty devices with instructions exact enough to build from.' 'the crankshaft joined to connecting rods, turning rotation into back and forth motion in his twin cylinder water pump.' 'His musical automata, drummers on a boat, kept rhythm with pegs set into a turning barrel; move the pegs and the rhythm changes.' 'his own book survives, in his own words, with his own paintings, one of engineering's great primary documents.'
research.retell: An engineer named Al-Jazari built a machine that turned a spinning wheel into a back and forth push using a crank and a rod, and cars still use that same trick today.

lines.text: Your car's crankshaft is 800 years old

lines.sub: An engineer, Al-Jazari, finishes his book

lines.text: His book explains 50 machines in detail
lines.sub: precise enough for someone to build

lines.text: A turning wheel drives a straight rod
lines.sub: rotation becomes a back and forth stroke

lines.text: The rod drives a twin cylinder water pump

lines.text: A program you could touch, centuries early
Your engine still turns his crank and rod
